Title: Federal Court judge criticises Najib's lawyers over late adjournment bid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A Federal Court judge today criticised Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers for making a last-minute attempt to postpone proceedings in his RM1.9 million civil suit against former attorney-general Tan Sri Tommy Thomas.
Justice Datuk Azimah Omar said Najib's legal team should have filed the application for an adjournment as soon as they knew he was on medical leave, to avoid wasting the court's time as judges had spent hours preparing for the case.
"If you already know that you are on MC on July 24 and you are serious enough to be present in court, you must submit (the adjournment application) on the day itself.
"This would have saved the judges' time. We have cases every day that we need to read. We took hours to read your files.
"The application for adjournment should be declined," she said.
Despite her objection, a three-member bench, in a 2-1 majority decision, allowed the former prime minister's oral application to adjourn the proceedings.
Court of Appeal president Datuk Abu Bakar Jais and Federal Court judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin formed the majority.
Earlier, Najib's lawyer Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin informed the court at the outset of the hearing that his client was unwell and wished to be present during the proceedings.
The hearing involved Najib's application for leave to appeal against the dismissal of his civil suit against Thomas.
It was recently reported that Najib had undergone a coronary angiogram.
Thomas' lawyer, Alan Adrian Gomez, opposed the application, arguing that Najib's attendance was unnecessary as the matter concerned only an application for leave to appeal.
When the court reconvened after a brief recess, Azmi said the court would grant the adjournment but made it clear that it would be the final one.
He reminded both parties that the matter would proceed on the next hearing date regardless of whether Najib was able to attend.
Firoz, when met after the hearing, said Najib had been granted medical leave until Aug 1.
"The new hearing date will be fixed later through case management," he said.
Najib, 73, filed the leave application on Feb 10 after the Court of Appeal upheld the High Court's decision to strike out his suit against Thomas.
He is seeking the Federal Court's permission to appeal on three legal questions and has also sought permission to file a notice of appeal within one month if leave is granted.
Najib filed the lawsuit on Oct 22, 2021, claiming Thomas had abused his powers and acted maliciously in initiating criminal charges against him in relation to the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC) cases.
Thomas served as attorney-general from June 4, 2018, to Feb 28, 2020.
Najib is seeking a declaration that Thomas committed the tort of misfeasance in public office and is claiming RM1.9 million in special damages, representing costs incurred to engage an audit team to review documents and prepare his defence in the criminal proceedings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: APHR: Myanmar not safe for Rohingya return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asean Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) co-chair Charles Santiago has questioned the plan to repatriate 5,000 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar.
He said Myanmar remains mired in a violent armed conflict, with the same military junta responsible for the original exodus still in power.
"Malaysia cannot, in good conscience, celebrate the return of 5,000 Rohingya to Myanmar without first answering one fundamental question: return them to what?" he said in a statement today.
The concern follows
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement
on Wednesday that Myanmar has agreed to take back 5,000 Rohingya currently in Malaysia, as part of a wider regional repatriation effort involving 300,000 refugees in Bangladesh.
He warned that without credible guarantees of safety, dignity, and citizenship, the move would be a "moral failure" rather than a diplomatic achievement.
He further cautioned that facilitating returns without transparent safeguards risks abandoning the humanitarian principles Malaysia has championed for decades.
Santiago also called on the government to see beyond the logistical challenges of hosting displaced persons.
On Monday, hundreds of Rohingya refugees gathered outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Jalan Bukit Petaling after allegedly being forced to leave their settlement in Penang.
All 113 Rohingya refugees were later relocated after undergoing overnight police screening and identity verification.
A total of 66 were relocated to Kuala Lumpur, 29 to Selangor and 18 to Penang

Title: 52 smuggled durian saplings seized, man arrested
Article:
TUMPAT: A 55-year-old man was arrested after the General Operations Force seized 52 durian saplings believed to have been smuggled from Thailand during an operation yesterday.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seizure was made by its Seventh Battalion, assisted by the Kelantan Agriculture Department.
He said the team intercepted a pickup truck along Jalan Jubakar in Kampung Kaki Itek at 3.45pm after finding it transporting the saplings without valid documentation.
"After inspecting the vehicle, the team uncovered 52 durian saplings suspected of carrying plant pests.
"The driver failed to produce the necessary documents for the plants, prompting authorities to detain him and seize the vehicle and cargo for further investigation.
"Initial investigations found that the saplings were destined for Kota Baru and surrounding areas," he said.
Radzi said the suspect was arrested and the case, together with the seized items, was handed over to the Kelantan Agriculture Department for further action under Section 6 of the Plant Quarantine Act 1976.
"Checks revealed this was the suspect's second arrest under agriculture laws.
"All seized saplings were found to be infested with pests or infected with disease and will be destroyed by the Agriculture Department through disposal and burial to prevent the spread of plant diseases," he said.

Title: Bursa Malaysia's Q2 net profit jumps 26pct, IPO target raised
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd's net profit jumped 25.9 per cent to RM71.78 million in the second quarter ended June 30 2026 from RM57.06 million a year earlier.
This prompted the exchange operator to raise its 2026 new listings' market capitalisation target to RM34 billion from RM28 billion.
Bursa Malaysia's revenue climbed 22.3 per cent to RM210.97 million from RM172.58 million.
The stronger performance lifted Bursa Malaysia's first-half net profit 15.2 per cent to RM144.61 million from RM125.48 million, with revenue rising 19.1 per cent to RM425.04 million.
Bursa Malaysia said the higher IPO target reflects robust fundraising activity and a healthy pipeline of prospective listings.
A total of 36 companies listed on the Main, ACE and LEAP Markets in the first half, raising RM5.4 billion and adding RM26.1 billion in market capitalisation.
"Reflecting the strong performance of the IPO market and a robust listing pipeline, Bursa Malaysia has revised upwards one of its 2026 headline KPIs, increasing its IPO market capitalisation target from RM28 billion to RM34 billion," it noted.
Bursa Malaysia's operating revenue rose 19.6 per cent year-on-year to RM411.7 million, driven mainly by stronger securities trading activity.
Its operating expenses increased 21 per cent to RM229 million, largely due to higher staff costs and regulatory fees.
Average daily trading value in the securities market jumped 35 per cent year-on-year to RM3.3 billion, while derivatives trading also strengthened.
Average daily contracts rose 9.9 per cent to 106,518, driven primarily by crude palm oil futures, which accounted for 84 per cent of total average daily contracts.
Bursa Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Fad'l Mohamed said geopolitical developments and external market uncertainties remained risks, but Malaysia's economic fundamentals continued to provide support.
He said the favourable 2026 growth outlook, supported by resilient domestic demand and continued expansion of the technology sector, should create a conducive environment for capital formation and investment.
"We are confident in the outlook for IPO activity in the second half of 2026, supported by a healthy pipeline and continued interest from companies seeking to raise growth capital through the public market," he added.

Title: Iran's IRGC says Strait of Hormuz cannot reopen while US 'threats' continue
Article:
TEHERAN, (Iran): Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Thursday that the Strait of Hormuz cannot be reopened as long as US threats and interference in regional maritime traffic continue, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"The Strait of Hormuz cannot be reopened as long as the bluster and threats of US officials and their interference in maritime movements in the region continue," the IRGC said in a statement.
It warned that continued "threats and interference" would make the situation "more difficult and complicated."
The IRGC claimed that two oil tankers, "at the instigation of US aircraft," attempted overnight to transit through what it described as an "unsafe route" south of the Strait of Hormuz.
It said both vessels quickly turned back after a major fire broke out aboard one of them.
"The Strait of Hormuz is our territory, and the IRGC Navy firmly controls it," the statement said, adding that no outside power "coming from thousands of kilometres away" would be allowed to interfere.
Earlier, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said American forces had carried out a "heavy wave" of strikes against Iran in response to what it described as attempted missile attacks targeting US forces in West Asia. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia weather agency warns El Nino to last through early 2027
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia recorded a sharp increase in potential fire zones in July as El Nino conditions intensified across the country, the head of the country's weather agency said on Thursday, adding that the weather system was expected to last into early 2027.
More than 5,000 hotspots were detected as of July 29, a sharp increase compared to previous El Niño years in 2015, 2019 and 2023, agency official Ardhasena Sopaheluwakan said in an online briefing.
The provinces of West Kalimantan, South Papua and Riau recorded the most hotspots.
As of mid-July 2026, 54.5 per cent of Indonesia's seasonal zones had entered the dry season, which is expected to peak in August, unchanged from a previous forecast, agency chief Teuku Faisal Fathani told the same briefing.
The risk of forest and land fires is expected to peak from August to September, particularly on the islands of Sumatra and Kalimantan, before gradually easing from October to November when higher rainfall is expected to return to some areas.
"The critical period for forest and land fires is expected from July through September 2026, making intensified monitoring and surveillance in high-risk areas crucial to prevent hot spots from spreading and causing wider environmental damage," Sopaheluwakan said.
Dry spells have been recorded across much of the country, with the longest stretch without rain reaching 80 days in Purworejo regency in Central Java.
There were 1,366 locations with dry spells lasting 21-30 days, 943 locations with 31-60 rainless days, and 70 locations where dry conditions persisted for more than 60 days.
The agency said hotspot activities have increased in West Kalimantan, heightening the risk of forest and land fires and driving dense haze concentrations.
The agency has conducted weather modification operations in several areas to reduce the risk of fires and limit their impact.
The agency had previously warned farmers to adjust their farming activities to mitigate risks stemming from the extreme dry weather expected this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four escaped Puspen inmates rearrested in Sungai Siput
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) has confirmed that four inmates who escaped from the Perlop Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) in Perak on July 24 have been rearrested.
Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said all four were detained in the Sungai Siput district with the assistance of police and local villagers.
Following the arrests, he dismissed a viral message claiming that the escapees were in the Bandar Baru Bangi area in Selangor and posed a danger to the public.
"The viral message is false as all four inmates escaped and remained within the Sungai Siput district before they were rearrested," he said in a statement today.
Ruslin said Nada had launched an internal investigation into the incident and would take disciplinary and legal action if any negligence or non-compliance with standard operating procedures was found among staff.
He urged the public not to spread unverified information, warning that those disseminating false news could face legal action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and other relevant laws.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amendments to Tabung Haji Act in the works following RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Stakeholder engagement sessions on proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 have been held following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the feedback and views gathered would be taken into account to ensure the proposed amendments were appropriate and effective.
However, he declined to disclose which provisions of the Act would be amended.
"We have taken note of the feedback and views from all parties to ensure the amendments are the most appropriate.
"Wait for it, InsyaAllah. We will table the amendments in the near future," he told reporters after the 2026 Zakat and Waqf Collection Agents Appreciation Ceremony.
He said the proposed amendments were among the RCI's 25 recommendations to strengthen Tabung Haji, with about 75 per cent of the recommendations already implemented.
Zulkifli also said several possible dates had been identified for a special Dewan Rakyat sitting to debate the report, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expected to announce the date.
Addressing concerns among depositors following the report's release, Zulkifli assured them that Tabung Haji remained in a strong financial position.
"What we want to tell our depositors is that one of our most important mandates is to safeguard the interests of our stakeholders, namely our depositors.
"So, depositors should not worry. Tabung Haji is now in a very good position. We can see that profits have increased and reserves have also grown," he added.
Yesterday,
the Cabinet declassified the RCI report
, which examined Tabung Haji's management and operations between 2014 and 2020, and agreed that it should be debated at a special Dewan Rakyat sitting.
The government also directed the police, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and Bank Negara Malaysia to investigate any elements of misappropriation, fraud or abuse of power identified in the report.
Among its findings, the RCI said the Tabung Haji Act 1995 required
a comprehensive overhaul
, as several provisions were no longer suitable.
The commission said the Act granted extensive powers to the minister responsible for Tabung Haji, including board appointments and removals, investments, hibah declarations and key operational matters. It found that this concentration of authority had weakened governance safeguards.
The RCI also recommended introducing statutory eligibility and professional requirements for board appointments, banning active politicians from serving on the boards of Tabung Haji and its subsidiaries, and removing the minister's sole authority to dismiss board members.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea's women web sleuths fight AI deepfake porn
Article:
UNDER banners emblazoned "Solidarity" and "We stand together with victims", a group of South Korean women digital detectives dredges the internet for a scourge of illegal AI-enabled pornography.
South Korea – home to the world's leading smartphone and memory chipmakers – takes huge national pride in its tech prowess.
But the success story has a dark side: women suffer rampant "digital sex crimes", rights groups say.
Spycams film them in private while chat groups blackmail them for explicit content and share so-called "revenge porn" without consent.
AI-generated deepfakes are the newest threat. Using the generative technology and a picture of their victim's face, harassers can fabricate invasive pornographic images portraying their targets.
At the National Center for Digital Sexual Crime Response – housed in an airy Seoul office – 23 women are tasked with turning the tide, trawling the web and filing delete requests backed by threats of legal action.
Last year, the group pulled down 318,000 videos and photos – deepfakes, spycam content and intimate imagery shared without consent – on behalf of 10,600 people, 75 per cent of whom were women and girls.
"South Korea acted faster than others because not only digital sex crimes became common earlier than elsewhere, but also women spoke out against them just as quickly and vigorously," Kim Mi-soon, the head of the government-founded centre, told AFP.
The centre opened in 2018, a year that saw tens of thousands of women demand action through anti-spycam protests.
The organisation's headquarters and 17 regional hubs also offer counselling and legal advice and collect evidence for prosecutions.
[[nid:1500379]]
One 33-year-old woman, who asked to be identified only by her surname Kim, said she had deepfakes shared in 2024 on encrypted apps beyond the reach of the centre's specialists.
"The centre may not be perfect, but it can make a huge difference for victims going through this nightmare alone," she said.
Kim, a member of the military, said she felt "healed" by their support – including financial aid to secure a trauma diagnosis for court evidence.
"It gave me a huge sense of relief and solace," she said.
"Navigating the whole legal procedure alone while suffering trauma would have been impossible."
Digital sex crimes are proving a mutable menace.
In 2020, the "Nth Room" scandal revealed men were exploiting dozens of women and girls they called "slaves" in pay-to-view "sextortion" chatrooms.
Since the 46-person national response centre was founded, sexual deepfakes have become the new trend.
Between 2019 and 2023, global deepfake circulation surged 550 per cent, according to web safety firm Security Hero.
Nearly 98 per cent of content was AI-generated pornography of women, with more than half the victims in South Korean, according to company research.
K-pop stars are main targets, but ordinary women are increasingly ensnared in a country where police data show digital sex crimes account for 40 per cent of all sexual offences.
"Since last year, we've seen more and more deepfakes of ordinary women and girls – with the images becoming way more sophisticated than before and victims getting younger and younger," said deletion specialist Kim Yun-hee.
[[nid:1500378]]
The centre uses its own AI tools, including a monitoring system capable of detecting exploitative material and messages targeting children.
"This job is not easy," the 31-year-old told AFP. "But it feels really rewarding whenever our clients say our service is a true life-saver."
Deepfake pornography is illegal in South Korea, with possession punishable by up to three years in prison and creators facing up to seven years behind bars.
Penalties were increased in 2024, the year a series of Telegram deepfake chatrooms were found to be sharing AI-generated sexualised footage of female acquaintances, classmates, colleagues and relatives, sometimes created from photos taken from victims' social media accounts.
Clare McGlynn, law professor at Britain's Durham University and an expert in image-based sexual abuse, said Seoul is "leading the way on providing holistic support services and investing in the latest technology to try to reduce the harm."
South Korea's approach offers "an example for the rest of the world", she told AFP.
Yet campaigners warn the problem's root cause is a patriarchal culture that regards women as sexual objects undeserving of dignity.
Kim Yeo-jin, head of the nonprofit Korea Cyber Sexual Violence Response Center, told AFP the online problem needs an offline solution.
"Unless we tackle this fundamental cause by fostering more gender equality in wider society and strengthening gender equality education at school, no amount of removal efforts will be enough," she said.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia and Japan launch postgraduate programme for Palestine students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) today signed an agreement to provide postgraduate education in engineering, science, and technology for Palestinian students under a six-year initiative starting October this year.
The initiative, which will run until April 2032, is expected to benefit between 15 and 20 Palestinian students.
Under the agreement, JICA will fund the scholarships, while UTM and its Malaysia-Japan International Institute of Technology (MJIIT) will provide research supervision, laboratory access, and academic support.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the rebuilding of Palestine must extend beyond restoring physical infrastructure to focus on developing human capital through higher education.
"The rebuilding of Palestine must not focus only on physical structures. It must also include the building of human capacity," he said in a speech read by Higher Education deputy director-general (Academic and Research) Prof Dr Zainal Amin Ayub.
Zambry said education was key to producing the engineers, researchers, educators, planners, and leaders needed to support Palestine's long-term recovery.
He said higher education institutions had a crucial role in equipping Palestinians with the skills needed to rebuild infrastructure, restore essential services, manage resources, and develop sustainable solutions.
He added that the strategic partnership would enable Palestinian students to pursue postgraduate studies and research at UTM MJIIT, reflecting the shared commitment of Malaysia and Japan to use education to address global challenges.
"Humanitarian assistance addresses the needs of today, and education builds the strength needed for tomorrow," Zambry said.
Earlier, UTM Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Mohd Shafry Mohd Rahim said the initiative extended the long-standing partnership between UTM and Japan toward supporting Palestine through education and capacity building.
Meanwhile, JICA President Dr Akihiko Tanaka described the agreement as an investment in Palestine's future, noting that human capital development was as vital as rebuilding physical infrastructure.
The agreement was signed during the launch of the "Malaysia-Japan Strategic Partnership: Engineering a Resilient Palestine" programme here.
Also present were Palestinian Ambassador to Malaysia Jehad Fouad Alqdra and Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man faces murder charges over fatal Teluk Intan crash
Article:
TELUK INTAN: A 28-year-old man was charged in the magistrate's court here today with four offences, including the murder of two schoolgirls in a crash near a secondary school on Sunday.
Alex Robert, a private sector employee in Singapore, was charged with murdering Nur Dania Arissa Salim, 17, and Nur Atikah Abdullah, 16, near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Seri Setia on Jalan Padang Tembak at 6.35pm on July 26.
No plea was recorded on the two murder charges as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The charges, framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carry the death penalty or imprisonment for between 30 and 40 years. If the death penalty is not imposed, the offender is also liable to no fewer than 12 strokes of the cane.
The accused was also charged with driving a Honda Civic under the influence of drugs, rendering him incapable of properly controlling the vehicle and causing injury to seven-year-old pedestrian Adam Arjuna Abdullah during the same incident.
He also pleaded not guilty to driving the same vehicle without due care and attention, resulting in an accident involving A. Suresh, 50.
The third charge, under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, carries a jail term of between seven and 10 years, a fine of between RM30,000 and RM50,000, and disqualification from holding or obtaining a driving licence for at least seven years upon conviction.
The fourth charge, under Section 43(1) of the same Act, carries a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000, imprisonment of up to 12 months, and an endorsement on the offender's driving licence.
The charges were read before magistrate Naidatul Athirah Azman, and the accused claimed trial.
Deputy public prosecutors Nasrul Hadi Abdul Ghani, Izzuddin Fakri Hamdan and Nur Darwis Aghniya Halim Azizi appeared for the prosecution, while counsel Koh Shean Wai represented the accused.
The prosecution applied for a new mention date to allow time to obtain the post-mortem reports of both victims, the accused's toxicology report and other related documents before the case is transferred to the High Court.
The court fixed Sept 11 for case mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman pleads not guilty to alleged fake payment receipt charge
Article:
KUANTAN: A housewife has claimed trial at the Magistrate's Court here today to a charge of allegedly submitting a fake payment receipt for RM8,998.
Nurwahidah Khamirrudin, 35, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Tuan Ruzuaini Tuan Lah.
The mother of two was accused of deceiving a 19-year-old woman by submitting a false payment transaction receipt.
The victim was allegedly tricked into handing over a gold bracelet with a butterfly pendant to a courier agent for delivery after being deceived by the false receipt.
The victim would not have surrendered the item had she not allegedly been misled in such a manner.
The offence was allegedly committed at a jewellery shop in Putra Square here at 10.40am on July 22.
The charge was framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years' imprisonment, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Siti Nabila Huda Jasmani proposed bail of RM7,000 with one surety, while National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Hakimie Ali represented Nurwahidah.
Hakimie pleaded for a lower amount, saying his client was supported by her security guard husband and had school-going children.
Tuan Ruzuaini set bail at RM5,000 with one surety and fixed Aug 20 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 8-year-old struggles to comprehend loss of parents, brother in Hulu Langat crash
Article:
KAJANG: The 8-year-old son of a couple killed in a crash in Hulu Langat yesterday is struggling to come to terms with the loss of his parents and three-year-old brother.
His grandfather, Rahmat Topani, 65, recalled the heartbreaking moment when the boy asked why he was performing the funeral prayers after the tragedy.
"He asked me why I was performing the solat jenazah. He did not understand what had happened.
"He initially believed his father (Hafifi), his mother and brother had been involved in a normal road accident and would be taken to hospital for treatment. But when we arrived at the cemetery, it finally sank in," Rahmat said when met at his residence in Kampung Jawa, Hulu Langat, here.
Hafifi is survived by his two sons, aged eight and 10.
Rahmat said the tragedy had forced him to adjust to a new reality after years of enjoying a quiet retirement.
"I am shocked. I have to change my daily routine. I was already used to my life as a retiree. Now, I have to find the strength to send my grandchildren to school."
He described Hafifi, the second of five siblings, as a kind-hearted mechanic who often allowed customers facing financial difficulties to pay for repairs later.
"He had his own workshop. If customers couldn't pay immediately, he never turned them away. He wasn't calculative."
Rahmat said his last meeting with Hafifi was the day before the crash, when the family visited his home.
"We had afternoon tea together. I even kissed my grandson who died in the crash."
Rahmat said the family would pursue insurance claims to help support Hafifi's two surviving sons.
Hafifi, his wife and their three-year-old son were killed after the motorcycle they were travelling on collided with a Perodua Aruz at Jalan Batu 17, Hulu Langat, yesterday morning.
Rahmat said Hafifi was on his way to send his son to kindergarten while his wife was heading to her business when the crash occurred.
Earlier, Dusun Tua state assemblyman Datuk Johan Abd Aziz visited the victims' family and presented contributions to them.
Johan said he personally knew Hafifi and his wife Nik Aishah Asilan Nik Mohd Zamzuri, describing the couple as generous individuals who never hesitated in their business dealings.
"I feel this loss deeply because we were quite close. Two months ago, during a gotong-royong programme, I met them. Hafifi and his wife sold steamed rice with spiced fried chicken, which was very delicious and popular in this area. It was also my favourite.
"I was shocked when I received the news yesterday. During Ramadan, he would always join us in programmes for residents. He would handle the wok and help fry the dishes for hours. We had become quite close," he said.
Johan said his office would assist with the education and welfare of the couple's two surviving children and help ease the burden on their grandfather.
He added that he would work with the relevant agencies to secure assistance, including legal aid if needed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 8 detained in Kota Baru operation following begging complaints
Article:
KOTA BARU: Eight people, including a nine-year-old girl, were picked up in a joint enforcement operation last night targeting homeless individuals and street beggars in Kota Baru.
Kelantan Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the operation was jointly carried out with the Kota Baru Municipal Council, the Immigration Department and the police.
He said the operation, led by council enforcement division chief Mohamad Ali, targeted homeless individuals and street beggars around Kota Baru, including areas near banks, Dataran Muhammadi and Dataran Bandaraya.
He added that enforcement officers also extended the operation to shopping centres in Kubang Kerian and Pasir Tumboh.
"Those detained comprised three Thai women, three Malaysian men and one Malaysian woman, aged between 48 and 70.
"The nine-year-old girl was found with her mother outside an ATM at a bank along Jalan Kebun Sultan. Her father is a Malaysian," he said.
Che Samsuzuki said the four Malaysian adults were detained under the Destitute Persons Act 1977, while the three Thai nationals were handed over to the Immigration Department for action under the Immigration Act 1959/63.
He said investigations found that the three Thai women, who were frequently seen selling snacks outside ATMs around the town area, were not genuinely conducting business but were instead relying on public generosity.
"Our investigations showed that they appeared to be selling snacks, but in reality they were using the activity to gain sympathy from people visiting ATM machines.
"Some of them are believed to earn as much as RM300 a day from donations and the kindness of members of the public," he said.
Che Samsuzuki added that the operation was launched following public complaints over the growing presence of foreign beggars along walkways outside several banks in the town area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother relieved as drink-driving suspect faces murder charge
Article:
KLANG: The mother of food delivery rider Zulfiqar Zamir Amirul Nizam said she felt a sense of relief after the man accused of fatally crashing into her son was charged with murder.
Hamidah Othman, 51, said the prosecution made the right decision after Zulfiqar died on May 25, 13 days after the alleged drink-driving crash.
"My family and I prayed that the accused would be charged with murder after my son died, and our prayers have been answered.
"I hope justice will be served. My son died senselessly," she said.
Hamidah and her family travelled from their home in Teluk Intan to attend the court proceedings in Klang, where Low Kean Peng, 35, was charged with murder.
Outside the courtroom, Hamidah broke down in tears as she spoke about her eldest son, the first of four siblings.
"He was the backbone of our family and took care of everything.
"He worked in Shah Alam but would return to Teluk Intan whenever he had the chance. Our lives have changed completely, and we miss him dearly," she said.
She said making the journey from Perak to Klang for every court hearing was not a burden.
"As long as my health permits, we will be here for every proceeding because I want to see justice served for my son."
Also present was Zulfiqar's fiancée, Nurul Syafiqah Ridzuan, 25. The couple had planned to marry in December before tragedy struck.
After the proceedings, Low's lawyer, Ethan W.H. Tan, said his client would be remanded at Sungai Buloh Prison while the case proceeds through the courts.
He said Low accepted the legal process and would allow the case to take its course.
It is understood that before being charged, Low broke down in tears and expressed concern about who would care for his elderly parents.
Low had previously pleaded not guilty to a charge of driving under the influence of alcohol and causing serious injuries to Zulfiqar.
Zulfiqar's death on May 25 prompted the prosecution to reclassify the case.
Low was accused of causing the death of Zulfiqar at 12.30am along Persiaran Kota on May 13.
The charge, framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carries the death penalty or jail of between 30 and 40 years upon conviction.
If the death penalty is not imposed, the offender must be whipped at least 12 times.
Earlier, Low, dressed in a white long-sleeved shirt and black pants, nodded and said he understood the charge after it was read before magistrate A. Khartiyayini.
No plea was recorded as the murder charge falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Zulfiqar, the eldest of four siblings, was on his way to deliver his final order of the night when he was allegedly struck by a Perodua Bezza driven by the accused.
The accused was believed to have been speeding while driving under the influence of alcohol from Port Klang towards Shah Alam.
He had allegedly driven against the flow of traffic for 3.5km before colliding with Zulfiqar, who was riding his motorcycle in the correct lane.
The impact threw Zulfiqar from his motorcycle, leaving him with severe injuries.
Police checks revealed that the accused had no prior criminal or drug-related records.

Title: Penang's Sungai Nibong TOD aims to reduce car dependency
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Limiting car dependency through efficient public transport, pedestrian-friendly design and parking controls will be key to the success of the proposed Sungai Nibong transit-oriented development (TOD).
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said concerns over worsening congestion along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah were understandable given the high-density development proposed for the area.
However, he said the TOD concept was specifically designed to reduce reliance on private vehicles by integrating residential, commercial and recreational developments with high-capacity public transport.
"If there was no public transport connectivity, yes, you're right. The roads would be completely jammed if we had such high-density development there.
"But the whole idea is to discourage people from using their cars. There is a carrot-and-stick approach. We encourage people by designing a system that is pedestrian-friendly and allows them to get everything they need within a five- to 10-minute walk," he said when responding to congestion concerns during a stakeholder engagement session on the Sungai Nibong TOD master plan here today.
Penang aims to transform Sungai Nibong into the state's first inclusive TOD, setting a benchmark for future rail-linked urban development.
The draft TOD master plan for Sungai Nibong is being positioned as more than a blueprint for development around the future Mutiara Light Rail Transit (LRT) Line.
Instead, the
state government envisions it as a model
for integrating transport, land use and community planning across Penang.
Zairil said Sungai Nibong was already an established transport hub with intercity and local bus services, while the upcoming Mutiara Light Rail Transit (LRT) line would transform it into a fully integrated multimodal interchange.
He said parking requirements for commercial and residential developments would also be reduced as part of efforts to discourage private vehicle use.
"People will drive if there is ample parking. But if parking is limited, they will be encouraged to use other options. If there was no alternative, then there would be a problem. But in this case, we have the LRT and buses," he added.
Zairil said that the Mutiara LRT line would comprise 21 stations, allowing commuters to use park-and-ride facilities at other stations instead of driving directly to Sungai Nibong.
"Even if you are driving from an area without LRT access, you can park at another station that is more convenient and take the train to Sungai Nibong. That's the whole idea of the network," he said.
Architect and urban planner Pranjali Deshpande, who is advising the project, said transit-oriented development should not be viewed simply as constructing taller buildings around rail stations.
Instead, she said, a successful TOD integrated land use, public transport, walking, cycling, public spaces and essential community facilities into a single planning framework centred on people rather than vehicles.
"In reality, TOD is not only about density. It is about creating a well-planned, integrated and people-centred urban environment," she said.
Pranjali said the Sungai Nibong proposal embraced the principles of inclusive TOD, ensuring accessibility for children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and families through universal design, quality public spaces and affordable housing opportunities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAP calls for immediate vape ban, says RM369mil health cost a waste
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers Association of Penang (CAP) has called for an immediate ban on vape products, saying the RM369 million annual cost linked to vape-related illnesses could be better spent on public health programmes.
CAP senior education officer NV Subbarow urged the government to stop delaying action and implement a total ban to protect public health.
"The RM369 million health cost is a waste. Go for a total vape ban and save the millions," he said today.
According to the Health Ministry, the health and economic costs arising from vape-related illnesses were estimated at RM369 million annually, exceeding the excise duty collected from vape products.
The ministry had said it was studying a proposal to ban bottled electronic cigarette liquids due to concerns that they could be modified or mixed with drugs or prohibited substances.
The ministry also said any
wider ban
would be assessed based on scientific evidence, current data and public health interests, while enforcement of the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 would be strengthened, particularly involving those below 18.
Subbarow said it was illogical for the government to spend millions treating vape-related illnesses when the issue could be prevented through a comprehensive ban.
He questioned the need for further evaluation, arguing that existing studies already provided sufficient evidence on the risks associated with vaping.
Subbarow said many countries had banned vaping to protect  younger generations.
He said Malaysia and the Philippines were among Asean member countries that had yet to impose a total ban on vape products.
Subbarow added that vape users spent about RM150 a month each on vaping.
He said the government should redirect resources used to manage vape-related health problems towards prevention efforts, such as health education campaigns.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Draft Sungai Nibong TOD master plan to be finalised by October
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The draft master plan for the Sungai Nibong transit-oriented development (TOD) is expected to be finalised by October, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today.
He said the state government is currently conducting stakeholder engagement sessions before finalising the conceptual master plan, with implementation expected to span between 10 and 15 years.
He said the next phase after completing the draft would focus on determining how the project would be implemented.
"At this stage, we are conducting stakeholder engagement and expect to complete this process by October, when the Sungai Nibong TOD concept will be finalised," he told newsmen said after the engagement session here today.
Penang is aiming to transform Sungai Nibong into the state's first inclusive TOD, setting a benchmark for future rail-linked urban development.
The draft TOD master plan for Sungai Nibong is being positioned as more than a blueprint for development around the future Mutiara Light Rail Transit (LRT) Line.
Instead the state government envisions it as a model for integrating transport, land use and community planning across Penang.
(Hyperlink: https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/07/1500251/penang-maps-out-inclusive-transit-hub-sungai-nibong)
Chow said implementation would involve deciding on project management, financing and the roles of the public and private sectors.
He said MRT Corp's responsibility would be limited to constructing the LRT depot and station at Sungai Nibong, while the remaining components would be undertaken by the state government as the land belonged to the state.
Chow said the conceptual master plan would require further refinement before implementation, including compliance with planning requirements, the provision of public amenities and housing guidelines.
"When we call for tenders to invite private sector participation, some of these components may have to be refined in accordance with our planning guidelines, the provision of necessary amenities and housing requirements.
"That is the next phase of turning this plan into a reality," he added.
He said the proposed development covered about 24 hectares, excluding the Penang Island City Council component, or about 27ha, including the council's land.
Sungai Nibong is selected because of its strategic location as a future multimodal transport hub, linking the Mutiara LRT Line with existing interstate and local bus services, while being close to the Penang International Airport, the Bayan Lepas industrial area and surrounding residential communities.
The area already serves as a key gateway to Penang and now presents an opportunity to evolve into a vibrant metropolitan destination in its own right.

Title: Trump's attorney general pick hits snag as key senator withholds support
Article:
WASHINGTON: Todd Blanche's bid for Senate confirmation as US attorney general faced a potential setback on Wednesday when Republican Senator John Cornyn cited unresolved concerns over a controversial US$1.8 billion fund tied to Trump allies.
Cornyn's concerns centre on provisions of President Donald Trump's settlement with his own administration, including a proposed US$1.8 billion "anti-weaponisation fund" for Trump's allies and an agreement that could give Trump and his associates protections from tax audits unavailable to ordinary taxpayers.
The dispute prompted Cornyn to cancel a meeting with Blanche ahead of a Senate Judiciary Committee vote scheduled for Thursday, with the Texas Republican saying he was not prepared to support the nomination until the Justice Department provided written assurances addressing his concerns.
Blanche, who served as Trump's personal defence lawyer before his second term, is already serving as acting attorney general, but he needs the backing of every Republican on the Senate Judiciary Committee to advance his nomination.
Cornyn's opposition could prove decisive.
"I'm not prepared to vote yes" on Blanche's nomination, Cornyn told reporters.
For his part the Republican Trump told reporters that he had thought Blanche's confirmation would be a routine process.
"Maybe John Cornyn's upset with me because I didn't endorse him," Trump said, referring to the senator having lost his primary runoff for another term to another Republican candidate endorsed by Trump.
Cornyn later called that a "convenient excuse."
Blanche submitted a proposal in writing on Wednesday to Cornyn and key Republicans that would "put the fund to bed," according to a person familiar with the matter, referring to the US$1.8 billion pot of money for Trump's allies.
Cornyn cancelled the meeting after he didn't receive a document responsive to his concerns. He is open to meeting once he receives that, his spokesperson said.
Blanche told lawmakers in May that he could not commit to barring money from going to people who assaulted police officers, including during the Jan 6, 2021, Capitol riot that sought to overturn Trump's 2020 election loss.
But he later told lawmakers the fund was not moving forward.
[[nid:1500333]]
The proposal would also clarify a related agreement signed by Blanche that gives Trump and his associates broad immunity from audits over his previous tax returns, the person said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly.
"I haven't seen a single piece of writing that is responsive to what I've requested," Cornyn told reporters.
He said that Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley had set a 4 pm (2000 GMT) deadline on Wednesday for deciding whether to cancel Thursday's meeting to vote on the Blanche nomination.
"There's plenty of time to resolve this," Cornyn said, although 4 pm came and went and no decision was announced. At about 6 pm, Cornyn said he was still not a yes, but a resolution could happen quickly.
Both the tax immunity agreement and the weaponisation fund emerged from a settlement agreement between Trump and his administration over the president's US$10 billion lawsuit against the tax-collecting Internal Revenue Service.
"I can see why he (Trump) wants it because it provides immunity from audits that no other taxpayer could possibly get," Cornyn said.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters on Wednesday that he thought Cornyn and the White House were talking to each other.
Cornyn and fellow Republican committee member Thom Tillis of North Carolina have expressed concern about Blanche's role in creating the fund.
Blanche needs both of their votes, and the votes of every other Republican on the committee, to advance the nomination to the full Senate.
Cornyn told reporters on Wednesday that his office sent the Trump administration his specific requests.
"They just need to make a decision," he said. "And if they do, then we'll proceed."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia slightly lower at midday amid geopolitical tensions, fed rate hold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia stayed lower at midday as renewed geopolitical tensions and the United States Federal Reserve's decision to stay pat on interest rates continued to dampen sentiment.
At 12.30 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 0.95 of-a-point to 1,714.61 from yesterday's close of 1,715.56.
The benchmark index opened 1.14 points lower at 1,714.42, before fluctuating between 1,710.69 and 1,716.95 during the morning trading session.
The broader market was negative, with losers outpacing gainers 553 to 299, while 528 counters were unchanged, 1,397 untraded and 87 suspended.
Turnover totalled 1.30 billion shares worth RM1.03 billion.
The US has launched strikes on Iran following an attack on a US military base in Jordan.
Meanwhile, the Fed has decided to hold rates steady for the fifth consecutive meeting, with the Federal Funds Rate unchanged between 3.50 per cent and 3.75 per cent. This also weighed on sentiment for the local bourse.
In a note today, Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd said three dissenting votes advocated for a 25 basis point rate hike.
The brokerage firm said Hengyuan Refining Co Bhd and Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd will benefit from prolonged supply disruption uncertainties in the Strait of Hormuz.
Among heavyweights, Tenaga Nasional eased four sen to RM14.56, CIMB shed one sen to RM7.80, and Public Bank dropped two sen to RM5.13. Maybank was unchanged at RM10.86, and IHH Healthcare inched up two sen to RM8.37.
Of the active stocks, Zetrix AI slid one sen to 69.5 sen, VS Industry shed 1.5 sen to 22 sen, SNS Network Technology and HHRG slumped half-a-sen each to 53.5 sen and 13 sen, respectively. Sum Technology added 3.5 sen to 62 sen.
As for the top gainers, Nestle advanced RM2.10 to RM98.88, Fraser & Neave Holdings jumped 36 sen to RM27.76, Kuala Lumpur Kepong rose 24 sen to RM21, Allianz Malaysia inched up 18 sen to RM21.18, and Westports Holdings climbed 15 sen to RM6.98.
Malaysian Pacific Industries led the losers list, falling RM1.06 to RM43.06, while United Plantations shed 16 sen to RM33.84, Riverview Rubber Estates lost 15 sen to RM3, Chin Teck Plantations declined 14 sen to RM10.90, and UMS Integration slipped 14 sen to RM6.86.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index decreased 14.09 points to 12,658.72, the FBM Top 100 Index inched down 13.22 points to 12,493.94, the FBM Mid 70 Index contracted 45.77 points to 17,935.86, the FBM Emas Shariah Index tumbled 3.01 points to 12,502.36, and the FBM ACE Index fell 11.33 points to 4,913.38.
Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index lost 29.64 points to 20,187.33, the Industrial Products and Services Index was unchanged at 186.33, while the Plantation Index gained 19.98 points to 9,321.90, and the Energy Index improved 3.23 points to 763.91.

Title: Jalaluddin: 10 more Orang Asli villages to be gazetted if BN wins
Article:
SEREMBAN: Another 10 Orang Asli villages in Negri Sembilan will be gazetted in the near future if Barisan Nasional m is given the mandate to form the state government in the Aug 1 state election.
Negri Sembilan Umno chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he is confident that the gazettement process can be completed within the first six months of the new administration.
The state BN deputy chairman and the coalition's state election director said the move is a continuation of BN's long-term commitment to restructuring and safeguarding the welfare of the Orang Asli community, a plan that has been implemented since 2013.
As a result, 58 of the state's 69 Orang Asli villages have already been gazetted.
"Some settlement boundaries overlap with permanent forest reserve areas. We need to realign those boundaries so we can resolve the issue.
"The Orang Asli community needs the government's attention. We cannot marginalise them in the administration of government, whether at the state or federal level," he said during the Bicara PRN Negri Sembilan.
Jalaluddin, who is also the member of Parliament for Jelebu, said he has consistently raised the concerns of the Orang Asli community in Dewan Rakyat, particularly on issues relating to living standards, housing, and economic opportunities for the younger generation.
He said that although many Orang Asli youths have attained higher education and are now working as teachers and lecturers, they continue to face difficulties obtaining housing financing because the land on which they live does not carry individual land titles.
"That is why we are fighting for them to be exempted from having to provide land as collateral when applying for housing loans or schemes such as Rumah Mesra Rakyat.
"From an economic standpoint, we are arranging organised agricultural plots through the state's agricultural agencies.
"If there are 42 families, we will establish 42 agricultural clusters so they can receive regular income, similar to shareholders receiving dividends," he said.
Commenting on the Felda community in the state, Jalaluddin said resolving inheritance issues affecting second- to fourth-generation settlers, providing legal assistance, and reviving abandoned Felda second-generation housing projects are among BN's key manifesto priorities.
He revealed that the nationwide plan to build 20,000 homes for second-generation Felda settlers, launched in 2012, came to a halt after BN lost the 2018 general election.
As a result, many housing projects that were 60 to 70 per cent complete were left abandoned.
"At that time, I was an opposition MP. The White Paper presented by the then economy minister had no meaningful impact in resolving this problem.
"The abandoned houses have become overgrown with vegetation, and the cost of restoring them is substantial. That is why this time we need a strong and stable state government, working closely with Felda's federal leadership, to resolve this long-standing issue," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt to expedite remaining 25pct TH RCI recommendations, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will expedite the implementation of the remaining 25 per cent of recommendations by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Tabung Haji, taking into account current realities and other relevant considerations.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the government was always open and ready to introduce changes while viewing the recommendations as an opportunity to further strengthen the institution.
"There is still much more that needs to be done to ensure that this institution, which we cherish, continues to soar higher," he told reporters after opening the Muzakarah Muamalat Kewangan Islam (MMKI) here today.
He said 75 per cent of the 25 recommendations submitted by the RCI had already been implemented, putting TH on the right track in managing haj deposits and operations.
This enabled the institution to receive the Diamond Award for the world's best haj management during the 1447H/2026M haj season.
On the recommendation to restructure TH's governance, Zulkifli said he was open to considering the proposal, including separating responsibilities for financial, fund, and investment management under the finance minister.
Zulkifli added that the recommendation to limit the scope of the religious affairs minister's authority to haj management was among the proposals contained in the RCI report published yesterday.
Yesterday, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) published the 211-page report on the investigation into TH's management and operational issues from 2014 to 2020, which contained recommendations to improve TH's operations.
On MMKI, he said the discourse was important to ensure Malaysia continued to remain among the world's leading countries in the Islamic Economy Index.
He said the platform brought together financial experts, academics, and industry practitioners to discuss current issues and examine global challenges to determine the direction of the country's Islamic finance sector.
Zulkifli said MMKI, initiated by Co-opbank Pertama (CBP), also served as a reference platform for industry players involved in Islamic banking and finance.
"This muzakarah will discuss current issues and today's realities, including developments taking place globally.
"Experts will provide their input and views, while also providing new information and data to Islamic banking practitioners and finance industry players, including CBP, to develop the best products, instruments, and solutions for the community," he said.

Title: BN to set up unit to monitor manifesto implementation, says Jalaluddin
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional will ensure every pledge in its election manifesto is fully implemented through a dedicated monitoring unit.
State Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said the manifesto implementation monitoring unit would be established immediately following the formation of the state government should the coalition secure a mandate in the Aug 1 election.
He said the unit would track the progress of manifesto commitments through regular reports tabled during state executive council meetings.
"The establishment of this unit shows BN is not treating the election merely as a platform to gain power by making unrealistic promises that cannot be fulfilled.
"When we present a manifesto, we must deliver on it. It has to be implemented in full so that the people receive everything we have promised during our term in office.
"We do not want to promise the impossible, such as monthly cash assistance of thousands of ringgit or free fuel, which are clearly unrealistic.
"BN's approach is to ensure every commitment is based on what the government is genuinely capable of delivering," he said during the Bicara PRN Negri Sembilan programme.
Jalaluddin said the state government would require at least RM30 million annually to implement the welfare programmes outlined in the manifesto.
He said the spending would be supported by stronger state revenue, allowing the government to channel the returns back to the people through initiatives benefiting all age groups.
Among the key pledges are RM200 assistance for senior citizens aged 65 and above, a RM200 contribution to the National Education Savings Scheme account for every newborn, and welfare aid for funeral expenses and patients with chronic illnesses.
To help ease the cost of living for lower-income families, BN also pledged higher education registration assistance of RM1,000 for degree students, RM750 for diploma students and RM500 for certificate students, as well as assistance for admission to fully residential schools.
Jalaluddin said young people would also benefit from a RM1,000 grant for first-time married couples to help them start married life.
He said the manifesto reflected a balanced five-year plan focused on economic development, public welfare, youth, heritage and the preservation of Negri Sembilan's customs and traditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teach Adibah Amin's works to foster unity, says former judge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The works of acclaimed Malaysian journalist, writer, and educator Adibah Amin should be incorporated into the school curriculum to instil values of unity, tolerance, and nationhood among younger generations, former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali said.
The Universiti Malaya Pro-Chancellor said Adibah's writings remained highly relevant as Malaysia continued to navigate issues of race, religion, and social cohesion.
"Currently, there is a seeming lack of understanding and tolerance of race and religion.
"If some agency can be moved to incorporate stories written by Adibah Amin in schools, as part of the curriculum, it will go a long way towards planting the seeds of nationalism in the hearts and minds of our children and young people," she said during her speech at "A Tribute to Adibah Amin: Book Reading" at Monash University Malaysia here.
Zainun described Adibah's book "As I Was Passing" as a precious collection whose significance would endure beyond the era in which it was written.
"It is not an understatement to say that Adibah Amin's collection of stories in 'As I Was Passing' is precious. Some stories are stories of the hour, whilst some are for all times. Adibah Amin's 'As I Was Passing' belongs squarely to the latter," she said.
The tribute brought together figures from journalism, literature, education, the arts, and civil society to celebrate the legacy of Adibah, who was unable to attend due to ill health.
A recipient of the Southeast Asian Writers Award, Adibah is widely recognised for her contributions as a journalist, novelist, educator, and translator. Her "As I Was Passing" columns, written under the pen name Sri Delima and published in the New Straits Times during the 1970s and 1980s, captured the humour, warmth, and humanity of everyday Malaysian life.
Monash University Malaysia President and Pro Vice-Chancellor Prof Emeritus Datuk Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman said the university was pleased to celebrate Adibah's work alongside Malaysia's rich literary and cultural heritage.
Although Monash is often viewed as a STEM-focused university, Adeeba said the institution also sought to embrace Malaysia's cultural diversity while celebrating the talents and achievements of Malaysians.

Title: Low Danube levels force nuclear shutdown in Romania
Article:
BUCHAREST: Romania will shut down its second nuclear reactor due to low water levels in the Danube, the energy ministry said Wednesday, days after the first was shut down for the same reason.
The two reactors at the Cernavoda plant run by Romania's national nuclear energy company Nuclearelectrica rely on the waters of the Danube for cooling.
"Given the unfavourable development of hydrological conditions on the Danube, Unit 2 of the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant will be shut down in a controlled manner tomorrow, July 30, starting at 10 am (0700 GMT)," the ministry said.
Nuclearelectrica said in a statement that the reactors were being shut down "in accordance with the plant's procedures applicable in situations of severe drought."
It is the first time both reactors have been shut down simultaneously due to low water levels in the Danube, according to local media.
The Danube – which runs from the Black Forest mountains of western Germany through 10 countries to the Black Sea – has dropped to record low levels in parts due to prolonged rain shortages and successive heatwaves since May.
Hungary has also reduced its nuclear output due to the river's low water levels.
Romania's acting prime minister Ilie Bolojan said the country would be forced to cover the energy shortfall by increasing production at gas-fired power plants and through imports, especially during peak consumption hours in the evening.
"I appeal to the citizens of Romania and large consumers to be mindful of their consumption during the evening hours, when we face an energy shortage," he told the Digi24 television channel.

Title: OCBC Bank commits RM325mil to battery storage project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OCBC Bank (Malaysia) Bhd has committed RM325 million to finance a utility-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project under the government's Battery Energy Storage (MyBeST) programme.
The financing will support a 100MW/400MWh BESS project by ERS Energy Sdn Bhd's unit ESS Bahau Sdn Bhd. The firm was one of four successful bidders selected by the Energy Commission under MyBeST, Malaysia's first competitive bidding programme for grid-scale battery storage.
OCBC Bank is the mandated lead arranger and facility agent for the project, which is expected to begin commercial operations in July 2027.
The RM325 million package includes project financing for the BESS facility as well as working capital for engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning works.
OCBC Bank head of wholesale banking Jeffrey Teoh Nee Teik said the financing reflects the bank's commitment to supporting Malaysia's energy transition and critical energy infrastructure.
"We are pleased to support ERS Energy in delivering one of Malaysia's first utility-scale battery storage projects, marking an important milestone in the country's energy transition journey," he said.
ERS Energy managing director Jonathan Kan said reaching financial close for the project marked a major milestone for the company.
He said the project would help strengthen grid reliability and support Malaysia's transition to cleaner energy.
The project supports the goals of the National Energy Transition Roadmap, which aims to raise renewable energy capacity to 70 per cent by 2050.
As at Dec 31, 2025, OCBC Bank had extended more than RM12 billion in green, social and sustainability-linked loans.
With battery storage required for initiatives such as the Large Scale Solar 6 and the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme, the bank said it is well placed to support growing demand for energy storage solutions in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two 19-year-olds remanded over newborn's death
Article:
KLUANG: Two students have been remanded for seven days over the death of a newborn baby girl who was found with stab wounds in a toilet bowl at a house in Taman Setia Mutiara here.
Magistrate Nurasidah A Rahman granted the remand order, effective today until Aug 5, to allow police to complete investigations.
The 19-year-old college students are being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder and Section 315 of the Penal Code for causing the death of a newborn child.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the female suspect is currently receiving treatment at Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital.
Earlier, Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police received a report at 1pm yesterday regarding
a female student
who was admitted to the hospital after allegedly giving birth.
He said medical examinations confirmed that the student had delivered a baby, while another baby girl was found in her womb.
"After giving birth, the student contacted her teacher before being taken to the hospital for examination.
"Further checks at the rented house where the student lived led to the discovery of the body of a baby girl.
"Initial examination found several stab wounds on the baby's body, although the actual cause of death remains under investigation," he said.

Title: Private hospitals association re-elects Dr Kuljit Singh for fifth consecutive term
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh has been re-elected as president of the Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) for a fifth consecutive term.
The decision was made at the association's annual general meeting today.
Under his leadership, APHM has continued to engage with government policymakers and key healthcare stakeholders on issues affecting Malaysia's private healthcare sector.
The AGM also saw the election of a new council to lead the association for the 2026–2028 term.
Joining Dr Kuljit in the executive line-up are vice-president Chin Keat Chyuan, honorary secretary Anwar Anis and honorary treasurer Erica Lam.
The newly elected council members are Dr Tan Hui Ling, Mohd Khairul Izzad Mohamed Shamsuddin, Poorani Ramachandran, Dr Seow Vei Kean, Dr Shuba Srinivasan, Tan Yew Aik and Stanley Lam.
APHM said the incoming council remained committed to advancing patient care, clinical standards, innovation and sustainable healthcare delivery across the country.
"In the coming term, APHM will prioritise the private sector's transition from volume-based to value-based healthcare, focusing on improving patient outcomes, driving quality and efficiency, embracing digital transformation, and supporting a more sustainable and patient-centred healthcare ecosystem," it said.
APHM said it would continue to work closely with the Health Ministry and government agencies to help shape policies aimed at strengthening the national healthcare system.

Title: Penang to decide on temporary venue for Pesta Pulau Pinang within weeks
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government will decide within weeks whether Pesta Pulau Pinang will be held at a temporary venue during the redevelopment of the Sungai Nibong site.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said discussions were ongoing with the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda) on a proposal to relocate the annual fair to Kubang Menerong in Seberang Perai Utara while construction of the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) depot and station takes place at the existing site.
He said the state government was considering several options before making a final decision.
"We are still discussing it. State Financial Office officials have been tasked with negotiating with Perda because there are several options," he told reporters after a stakeholder engagement session on the Sungai Nibong transit-oriented development (TOD) master plan today.
It was previously
reported
that Pesta Pulau Pinang would take a six-year hiatus to make way for construction of the LRT line.
Pesta Pulau Pinang was introduced under the leadership of Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, who served as Penang chief minister from 1969 to 1990.
Launched in 1970, the annual fair was conceived to stimulate business activity and provide economic opportunities amid high unemployment and a challenging economic environment.
Held during the year-end school holidays, it became known for showcasing consumer products, commercial exhibits and family-friendly attractions.
The event did not have a permanent home in its early years, moving between venues including the Esplanade and Lebuh Macallum before relocating to Sungai Nibong in 1974.
Elaborating, Chow said the first option was not to hold Pesta Pulau Pinang during the construction period.
He said the second option was to continue staging the fair on the remaining land at Sungai Nibong that would not be affected by the construction.
However, he said the state executive council did not consider this appropriate as the site would be adjacent to active construction works.
"The third option is to hold the fair at another location. We have received a proposal from Perda and feel it is more suitable as a short-term arrangement," he said.
Chow said a final decision would have to be made soon to give organisers sufficient time to prepare for the annual event.
"We have to make a final decision so that there is sufficient time to organise the yearly Pesta Pulau Pinang at another proposed site.
"So we will have to make a decision probably within weeks — one week, two weeks or three weeks," he said.

Title: Rohingya activist urges Asean to halt repatriation until Myanmar is safe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia has urged Asean member states, including Malaysia, not to repatriate Rohingya refugees until what it described as the "ongoing genocide" in Myanmar is resolved.
He told the New Straits Times that while the Rohingya community wanted to return home, the ongoing conflict in Rakhine State meant any forced repatriation would amount to a "death sentence".
"The refugees I spoke to are distraught. They have no homes left. Everything has been reclaimed by the military junta.
"We have no citizenship, safety or dignity there," said Zafar, 56, president of the Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia.
His remarks followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement on Wednesday that Myanmar had agreed to repatriate an initial group of
5,000 Rohingya refugees
currently in Malaysia.
Zafar recently said Malaysia had shown sympathy towards the Rohingya through humanitarian assistance, advocacy and efforts to raise awareness internationally.
He said Malaysia had raised the
Rohingya issue
at international forums, including Asean and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, while Malaysian organisations had also provided aid and expressed solidarity with the Rohingya community.
Zafar said that instead of deporting Rohingya refugees, the government should allow them to help address labour shortages.
"The Rohingya refugees are not a burden. Many are already working in the construction and agriculture sectors, which are shunned by locals," he said.
Addressing rising xenophobia, Zafar blamed AI-generated fake news for spreading false claims that the community was demanding land rights.
He also cited data released by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail showing that only 0.02 per cent of crimes in Malaysia
involved Rohingya refugees,
which he said contradicted claims that they posed a security threat.
In a direct appeal to Asean member states, Zafar called for the "responsibility to protect" principle to be applied, saying any future repatriation should take place only under the protection of United Nations peacekeepers in designated safe zones.
"The fear is so great that many would rather face the end here."
Most Rohingya fled Myanmar during a military crackdown in 2017, with many seeking refuge in neighbouring countries, including Bangladesh and Malaysia.
The military operation, which involved villages being burned and civilians killed, is the subject of a genocide case before the United Nations' top court in The Hague.
Myanmar has maintained that the Rohingya are descendants of migrants from Bangladesh and that the 2017 operation targeted a militant uprising.
